title: VC Dimension of Interval Classifiers on ℕ

problemStatement.informal: What is the VC dimension of interval classifiers H = {[a,b] | a,b ∈ ℕ} on ℕ?
problemStatement.formal: Prove VCDim(intervalClassifiers) = 2, i.e., (1) ∀ p q, p < q → Shatters H {p,q} and (2) ∀ a b c, a < b → b < c → ¬Shatters H {a,b,c}.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: Proved by researcher-3 on feature/researcher-3. intervalClassifiers has VC dimension exactly 2: intervals shatter every pair (4 explicit witnesses), but no ordered triple (convexity obstruction forces middle point in). 3 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
insights: Key obstruction: any interval [lo,hi] containing outer points a and c of a < b < c must contain b by transitivity: lo ≤ a < b < c ≤ hi
Empty interval trick: [q+1, q] = ∅ since q+1 > q — no special empty-class constructor needed
Comparison: threshold classifiers have VC dim 1 (one free parameter), intervals have VC dim 2 (two free parameters: left and right endpoint)
General pattern: k-interval classifiers on ℕ should have VC dim 2k (each interval contributes 2 degrees of freedom)
builtItems: intervalClassifiers: definition of interval hypothesis class {x | a ≤ x ∧ x ≤ b} in PACLearningOQ01OQ01.lean
interval_shatters_pair: every 2-element set {p,q} with p<q is shattered by 4 explicit intervals
interval_not_shatters_triple: no ordered triple {a,b,c} is shattered (convexity obstruction)
nextSteps: Prove VCDim of k-interval classifiers on ℕ is 2k (generalization)
